interest: Shows Siam's postwar effort, aided by SCAP intelligence, to gather evidence against a Japanese wartime propagandist for war crimes.
overview: 1946 correspondence on Yao Suthinun, a Siamese who produced Japanese wartime propaganda against Thailand; Tokyo intelligence findings prompted Siam's War Crimes Commission to seek his whereabouts and evidence.

people.name: Yao Suthinun
people.role: Siamese national employed by the Japanese Government to conduct wartime propaganda aimed at Siam

people.name: Charles W. Yost
people.role: U.S. Chargé d'Affaires / Diplomatic representative at the American Legation in Bangkok

people.name: N. Lancaster, Jr.
people.role: Diplomatic officer and drafter at the American Legation in Bangkok

subfiles.about: Reports intelligence on Yao Suthinun, a Siamese national who conducted wartime propaganda in Japan, and suggests notifying the Siamese Government.
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser / SCAP (Tokyo via War Department)
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 63: Tokyo's Counter-Intelligence Section reports Yao Suthinun was paid by Japan to produce wartime propaganda for Siam.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 63 from Tokyo regarding Propaganda Activities of Yao Suthinun

subfiles.about: Transmits a request from the Siamese Foreign Office and War Crimes Commission for evidence regarding Yao Suthinun's whereabouts and collaboration with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-5: Bangkok reports Siam's War Crimes Commission seeks Yao Suthinun's whereabouts and proof of his Japanese propaganda work.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-5 from Bangkok regarding War Crimes Commission Inquiry on Yao Suthinun
